title: Editorial Sign-off
description: Human sign-off on the EDITORIAL content warnings (real-evidence coverage, generic-card usage, emphasis-beat pacing) of one specific frozen candidate, modeled on schemas/proof_approval.schema.json's identity-hash pattern. proof_approval.json approves that the candidate is technically the one a human reviewed; this file approves that a human has actually read the current editorial QA warnings for that same candidate and accepts them -- automated QA (scripts/orvyq_real_asset_coverage_audit.mjs, orvyq_generic_card_audit.mjs, orvyq_tension_card_audit.mjs) intentionally treats coverage/margin/pacing shortfalls as warnings rather than hard failures, to avoid blocking legitimate creative choices in CI -- but that means nothing anywhere previously required a human to have actually seen them. This also concretely fulfills orvyq_alignment_score.mjs's own long-standing qa/alignment_readiness.json.human_rendered_video_review ({required: true, status: 'pending'}), which nothing has ever read back or transitioned. This schema, and scripts/orvyq_verify_approval.mjs's verifyEditorialSignoff(), close that gap the same way verifyApprovalRecord() already closes it for technical identity: candidate_hash ties this record to one exact qa/frozen_candidate.json, so any re-edit/re-render invalidates it automatically, and acknowledged_warnings must list every warning string those reports currently produce, so a NEW warning introduced later cannot silently ride on an old sign-off.

candidate_hash.description: The signed-off frozen candidate's own canonical_candidate_identity-derived candidate_hash field -- same field proof_approval.json uses, not a whole-file hash.

candidate_source_sha.description: The source commit SHA the signed-off candidate was built from (canonical_candidate_identity.source_commit_sha), carried for the same consistency-only reason as proof_approval.json's field of the same name -- never compared against the current git HEAD.

reviewer.description: Identity of the human who reviewed the editorial warnings (name or email), not an automated actor.

acknowledged_warnings.description: Verbatim copies of every warning string currently produced by qa/real_asset_coverage_audit.json, qa/generic_card_audit.json, and qa/tension_card_audit.json at the time of review. verifyEditorialSignoff() fails if any warning those reports currently produce is not present here -- a warning introduced after this sign-off was recorded must be reviewed again, not inherited silently.
